name: Semyonovskoye Gorge
near: Semyonovka — a village on the north-shore highway at the mouth of the gorge (the Kichi-Ak-Suu gorge opens 4 km above the village — Nomad's Land); Grigorievka, 4 km to the west — the entrance to the neighbouring Chon-Ak-Suu. Kojoyar (OSM, 3.9 km) is the nearest marker to the catalogue point, but access is via Semyonovka.
elev: Gorge entrance ~1,900 m (Nomad's Land); Kyrchyn jailoo (summer pasture) ~2,100 m (eurasia.travel: the Kichi-Ak-Suu area ~2,100 m); Lake Sut-Bulak 2,450 m; Sut-Bulak Pass 3,924 m; peaks up to 4,260 m.
short: The most popular gorge on the north shore of Issyk-Kul: 30–35 km of spruce valley along the Kichi-Ak-Suu river above the village of Semyonovka, summer yurt camps on the Kyrchyn jailoo, horse rental, Lake Sut-Bulak; since 2026 a new paved road to Kyrchyn, the venue of the World Nomad Games.
desc: The gorge is named after P. P. Semyonov-Tian-Shansky and lies 40 km east of Cholpon-Ata on the southern slope of Kungey Ala-Too. From the village of Semyonovka the road climbs along the turbulent glacial Kichi-Ak-Suu river through spruce woods with barberry, sea buckthorn and currant to the broad Kyrchyn jailoo, where several rivers meet and where in summer yurt camps are set up with kumys and beshbarmak, horse rental and golden eagles for photos. Higher up is the “sacred” Lake Sut-Bulak (2,450 m) and passes to the Grigorievskoye (Chon-Ak-Suu) gorge: at the head the two valleys join, so tours usually do a “Grigorievskoye — Semyonovskoye” loop. Kyrchyn is the ethnopark of the World Nomad Games (2016, 2018, 2026): for the Games of 1–6 September 2026, 35.5 km of road to the jailoo were paved, parking and fences were installed. At the entrance there is a barrier and a “modest eco fee” (eurasia.travel); 2GIS says “free entry”. Access year-round, in winter — ski slopes.
guide: If you have one day for the mountains on Issyk-Kul — take Semyonovskoye: since summer 2026 fresh asphalt leads to the Kyrchyn jailoo, and an ordinary car reaches the yurts. It is better to do the loop: go up via Grigorievskoye (steeper and narrower), cross the pass and come down via Semyonovskoye — this is what all the local guides show. At Kyrchyn take a horse for half an hour to an hour (a guide — 100 som for 10 minutes in 2024–2025), try kumys and shashlik in a yurt, but do not count on low prices — they are resort prices. If you have the energy, climb to Lake Sut-Bulak (2,450 m). On weekdays and in June there are many times fewer people than in August; on weekends in season there are traffic jams at the entrance.
see: Spruce slopes and the Kichi-Ak-Suu river; the Kyrchyn jailoo with yurt camps and the nomad games ethnopark; Lake Sut-Bulak (2,450 m) — a side trip up; the pass into the Grigorievskoye gorge with views of the lake; eagle handlers and horse rental; in winter — ski slopes at the Kyrchyn tourist base.
skip: You are looking for untouched nature — in July–August this is the busiest gorge on the north shore. You are already planning Grigorievskoye: the landscape is similar and they are usually combined in one trip. You dislike “touristy” yurts with resort prices.
diff: Easy: to Kyrchyn — by car; walks on the jailoo — no elevation gain. The side trip to Lake Sut-Bulak (2,450 m) — moderate, a few hours. Pass routes into Grigorievskoye — for the prepared (Sut-Bulak Pass 3,924 m).
when: The yurt camps run from late June/July to the end of September (too.kg: late July — late September; issykkul.biz: late June — late September). June — snowfields and greenery, August — peak; September — quiet and golden autumn. In winter there is access (eurasia.travel), skiing. On 1–6 September 2026 private-vehicle access was closed (World Nomad Games).
hours: Open terrain, around the clock; the barrier at the entrance works in daylight (eurasia.travel). Yurts — seasonal, daytime; the Kyrchyn tourist base — year-round.
daytime: First half of the day: tours from Cholpon-Ata start at 9:00–9:30, and by lunch Kyrchyn peaks; leave earlier or arrive after 15:00, when the groups leave. In the afternoon in summer thunderstorms are frequent.
how: From the Bishkek — Karakol highway (A363) in the village of Semyonovka (40 km east of Cholpon-Ata) turn south into the mountains; 35.5 km of road to the Kyrchyn jailoo were paved in 2026 (economist.kg, 20.07.2026). Marshrutkas (minibuses) Cholpon-Ata/Bosteri — Semyonovka/Grigorievka along the highway, then a taxi or on foot uphill (from the village to Kyrchyn ~15 km). From Bishkek ~4–5 h.
needcar: Yes: from the highway to Kyrchyn it is ~15 km; there are no regular marshrutkas in the gorge (free buses ran only for the World Nomad Games 2026). A passenger car manages the new road; for the upper reaches and the loop via Grigorievskoye — a 4×4.
self: Yes: the road has signs, no permits; at the entrance a barrier with an eco fee. Independently it is convenient in your own/rented car; on foot from Semyonovka it is long (15 km uphill).
roadtype: Paved from the highway to the Kyrchyn jailoo (35.5 km renovated and paved by July 2026 — economist.kg); previously issykkul.biz: ~15 km of paved road from the village, then dirt. Above Kyrchyn and over the pass into Grigorievskoye — dirt, 4×4 (2GIS: “a passenger car can pass, a 4×4 is recommended”).
traveltime: Cholpon-Ata — Semyonovka ~40 min; Semyonovka — Kyrchyn ~30–40 min on the new road; a tour with the loop via Grigorievskoye — 10 h (Tripster/Sputnik8). A walk in the gorge — 2 h (ru_travel).
stay: Yurt camps at Kyrchyn (an overnight in a yurt with meals is part of Tripster tours; prices are not published separately), the Kyrchyn tourist base (year-round — eurasia.travel), guesthouses in Semyonovka/Grigorievka, the Ananyevo and Bosteri guesthouse resorts. Specific 2025–2026 prices not found.
net: In May 2026 Beeline KG installed new base stations “in the Semyonovskoye gorge (Kyrchyn)” and in the villages of Ornok, Chok-Tal, Kojoyar, Frunze (economist.kg, 25.05.2026) — Beeline coverage exists in the Kyrchyn area; other operators — not confirmed; do not expect coverage above Lake Sut-Bulak.
entry: Contradictory: 2GIS — “free entry”; eurasia.travel — a barrier at the entrance and a “modest eco fee” (amount not stated). Separate paid services: horses, a golden eagle for photos, yurts. Check on site; a guide from similar places in the region — 50–200 som per car.
transfer: Tour from Cholpon-Ata: 700 som (group of 7–14) / 900 som (3–6) per person (issykkul.biz, date not stated); Tripster 4×4 €250 per car for up to 6 people (2025); Sputnik8 $230 per group (2024 archive). Horse — 100 som/10 min. Lunch in a yurt — from 600 som (Sputnik8).
bring: A windbreaker and a warm layer (Kyrchyn is 500 m higher than the lake, cold in the evening), sun protection, cash (yurts, horses, eco fee), water, swimwear for Ak-Bermet on the way, trekking shoes for Sut-Bulak.
warn: Do not confuse them: the Semyonovskoye gorge starts from the village of Semyonovka (Kichi-Ak-Suu), the Grigorievskoye from Grigorievka (Chon-Ak-Suu); guidebooks mix them up. Prices in the yurts are resort prices (ru_travel). During mass events at Kyrchyn (nomad games) private-vehicle entry is closed. Thunderstorms after lunch, the river is glacial — do not swim. Photos with a golden eagle/eagle cost extra, and the animals are not always kept humanely.
food: In the Kyrchyn yurts: kumys, beshbarmak, kuurdak, shashlik, boorsok, apiary honey (too.kg, issykkul.biz, ru_travel); lunch in a yurt from 600 som (Sputnik8). Trout from the Ak-Suu — in cafes by the highway. Specific yurts were not checked.
reviews: 2GIS “Semyonovskoye Gorge (Kyrchyn)”: 4.9/5, 320 ratings, 73 reviews (07.10.2026). Google Maps: 4.8/5, 73 ratings (03.10.2026). Tripster (tour): 4.89, 35 reviews. Pros: accessibility, spruce and river, yurts, horses; cons: crowds in season, inflated prices in the yurts, dirt road above Kyrchyn.
p.sum: The simplest mountain outing on the north shore: from the A363 highway in the village of Semyonovka (≈40 km east of Cholpon-Ata) turn south; since summer 2026, 35.5 km of road to the Kyrchyn jailoo are paved, so an ordinary sedan gets there. Without a car — a marshrutka along the highway to Semyonovka and a taxi up, or a tour from Cholpon-Ata (700–900 som per person in a group; 4×4 €250 per car). At Kyrchyn — yurts with lunch (from 600 som), horses (100 som/10 min), a short climb to Lake Sut-Bulak (≈3 km, +400 m). Stay overnight in a yurt at Kyrchyn, the Kyrchyn tourist base or the guesthouse resorts of Chok-Tal/Bosteri.

p.season: May–June — greenery and snowfields, ticks in the spruce woods; July–August — peak, weekend traffic jams, yurts operating; 1–6 September 2026 — World Nomad Games (private-vehicle entry was closed); September — quiet, golden; October–April — the Kyrchyn tourist base, skiing in winter, no yurts.
p.budget.economy: Marshrutka Bishkek — Cholpon-Ata 400–600 + along the highway to Semyonovka ~100; group tour 700–900; lunch 600; horse 100/10 min; guesthouse from 500–600. ≈ 2,500–3,500 som per person per day.
p.budget.comfort: Taxi Bishkek — Cholpon-Ata ~7,000 per car or a 4×4 tour €250 (÷4 ≈ 6,000 som); guesthouse resort 1,800–3,000 with meals; lunch in a yurt, Ak-Bermet 350. ≈ 9,000–12,000 som per person.
p.permits: No border-zone permit needed. At the entrance a barrier with an eco fee (eurasia.travel; amount not published), 2GIS — “free entry”. Pay in cash on site.
p.access: Excellent for children and older people: paved road to the yurts, a flat jailoo, toilets at the parking areas (2026). Stroller — on the asphalt and at the parking areas; the climb to Sut-Bulak — no. With a dog — allowed, herders’ dogs by the yurts.
